clue.text: Red with feelings stirred up about possessing wealth

definitions.text: Red with feelings stirred up about possessing wealth

indicators.note: about possessing means the jumbled letters sit around, and so hold, the next piece
stirred up means the letters of red and feelings are mixed into a new order

parts.note: wealth taken adjectivally: someone with wealth is rich

explanation.surface: A passionate communist, though a wealthy one, is described.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: Engels was the son of a rich mill-owner and paid Marx's way, a wealthy Red.
explanation.definitionFit: The German co-author of the Communist Manifesto was a committed socialist, yet a wealthy businessman, so a Red who possessed riches.

clue.text: Where you could find jacks — there should be sixteen of them here, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the phrase before it is to be said aloud, matching another spelling

parts.words: there should be sixteen of them here
parts.note: each pack of cards holds four jacks, so sixteen jacks need four packs, four decks

explanation.surface: Someone muses on where sixteen jacks might be found.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacks are both playing cards and the small flags flown at a ship's bow; a pack of cards is a deck.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack is a small flag flown at a ship's bow, so it is found on the forward part of the deck.

clue.text: Queen enters wearing robe digging into flesh

parts.note: someone wearing a garment is in it

indicators.note: enters means the queen's letter goes inside the word for robe

parts.note: a robe is a gown
R, for Regina, is the usual abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A queen arrives in her robes of state.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingrown toenail is one that has grown into the flesh around it, so it digs in.

clue.text: Suppliers of humbug and fudge consumed by medics

indicators.note: consumed by means the word for fudge is swallowed inside the medics' letters

parts.note: DRS, short for doctors, are medics
to fudge an issue is to dodge or elude it

explanation.surface: Doctors scoff a box of fudge.
explanation.walkthrough: Humbug and fudge both look like sweets here; humbug is deception, and fudge is a verb meaning to evade.
explanation.definitionFit: Humbug is deceptive talk, so those who supply it are people who deceive, deluders.

clue.text: Place to save a designated victim

parts.note: an ISA, an Individual Savings Account, is a British tax-free savings account, a place to save money
a is read as a/c, the usual abbreviation for account, so the savings place becomes an ISA account

explanation.surface: A savings account is set aside for someone singled out for loss.
explanation.walkthrough: ISA A/C reads as an ISA account, so 'a' gives A and C stands for the account. An ISA is a UK tax-free savings account.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Abraham's son was the boy chosen to be sacrificed on the mountain before God spared him, a victim marked out in advance.

clue.text: They keep drinks cool, with loud requests to swallow litre

parts.note: hip means fashionable, cool
F, forte, is the musical direction for loud
requests are asks

explanation.surface: Coolers for drinks are noisily demanded, a litre at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep drinks cool' reads as one phrase about refrigeration, but cool belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Small flat flasks carried in a pocket hold spirits, so they are containers that keep drinks.

clue.text: Scoffed in compiler's absence?

parts.note: absence of something means there is no such thing
the compiler's place of work, a garden shed, the classic writer's retreat

explanation.surface: Someone ate the lot while the setter was away.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'in compiler's absence' as NO SHED, the compiler's workplace being a shed; 'in' is a link. The question mark flags the playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is slang for food, so to nosh is to eat heartily, the same as scoffing.

clue.text: Company offering record value in Dubai?

parts.note: EMI is a British record company
a rate is a value or price

explanation.surface: A music firm offers a recording deal in the Gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai is one of the seven United Arab Emirates, a state ruled by an emir; the question mark marks an example.

clue.text: Victory in Berlin with English military operation

parts.note: Sieg is the German word for victory

explanation.surface: A wartime victory in the German capital is won alongside the English.
explanation.definitionFit: Surrounding a town to force its surrender is a classic military operation.

clue.text: Cracking booze knocked back, very fine stuff

indicators.note: knocked back, like a drink downed, here means the two pieces are read from end to start

parts.note: A1 (written AI) means first-rate, cracking
lager is booze

explanation.surface: Great beer, downed in one, is the finest thing there is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' turns the whole charade round. It looks like downing a drink, but here it signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are the emblems and splendid robes of royalty or office, so they are very fine stuff.

clue.text: Utter fool's ebbing interest

indicators.note: ebbing, flowing back like a tide, means both pieces are read backwards

parts.note: to utter is to emit a sound
a sap is a fool

explanation.surface: A complete idiot's enthusiasm is waning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective (complete) but is a verb. 'ebbing' turns EMITSAP round.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobby is an activity you take an interest in, a pastime.

clue.text: Report of outstanding au pair

indicators.note: report of means what follows is spoken and heard as another spelling

parts.note: money outstanding is due; au, French for to the, is said like the letter O

explanation.surface: A complaint about an excellent nanny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'au pair' looks like the live-in helper, but au is spoken as OH, and pair alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A duo is a set of two, as in a musical double act, the same as a pair.

clue.text: It exposes bust company during depression, say, worried for turnover

indicators.note: during means the company letters sit inside the hollow

parts.note: a dell is a small wooded hollow, a depression in the land

indicators.note: for turnover means the two pieces are turned round

parts.note: EG, for example, is what say means
ate, as in what's eating you, means worried

explanation.surface: A firm going bust in a slump has its turnover worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for turnover' turns the second pair of pieces round to give ETAGE. 'bust' and 'turnover' look like business terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A low neckline on a dress reveals the bosom, so it exposes the bust.

clue.text: This is a massive fiddle, 80% black market and extremely suspicious

indicators.note: 80% means only the first eight of the word's ten letters are kept

parts.note: contraband is goods traded on the black market

indicators.note: extremely means take the extreme letters of the following word

explanation.surface: A big racket, mostly smuggled goods and very fishy.
explanation.walkthrough: '80%' keeps eight of CONTRABAND's ten letters, CONTRABA; 'extremely' takes S and S. 'fiddle' looks like fraud but is the violin.
explanation.definitionFit: The double bass, the largest of the violin family, is also called by this name, so it is a huge fiddle.

clue.text: Ruler at sea is in second class, travelling in a train

parts.note: B is the grade below A, second class

indicators.note: travelling means the letters of in a train move about

explanation.surface: Someone rides second class on a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' scrambles IN A TRAIN to RITANNIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The song Rule, Britannia! says this figure rules the waves, so she is the ruler at sea.

clue.text: Man joining Nazis

parts.note: he is a man, the masculine pronoun
SS, the Schutzstaffel, were Nazi paramilitaries

explanation.surface: A man signs up with the Nazi party.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines Rudolf Hess, Hitler's deputy, who joined the Nazis early.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Hess was a man who joined the Nazi party early and became Hitler's deputy.

clue.text: Broadcaster, rich man, grabbing right to show high level sportspeople

parts.note: Sky is a British broadcaster

indicators.note: grabbing means the rich man's name holds the right letter inside it

parts.note: Dives is the rich man in the Bible's parable of Lazarus

explanation.surface: A media tycoon seizes the rights to televise a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who jump from aircraft and fall before opening parachutes do their sport at great height.

clue.text: Tasteless headline from Sun: "Best woman's going topless"

parts.note: the cream is the best part

indicators.note: going topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: her is what belongs to a woman

explanation.surface: A tabloid splashes a lurid headline about a woman baring her chest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid. 'going topless' drops H from HER to leave ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A screamer is a sensational banner headline in big type, the tabloid kind called tasteless.

clue.text: Pop has trouble with son about

indicators.note: about means the word for trouble is turned round

parts.note: ado is fuss, trouble

explanation.surface: A father has bother with his boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the trouble word round. 'Pop' looks like a dad but means fizzy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop is fizzy drink, and soda water is one.

clue.text: Hell! It's the wrong colour

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, hell
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Someone swears at a paint shade they hate.
explanation.definitionFit: To colour an account is to slant or bias it, giving a false picture.

clue.text: Notion Tory created by egoistic fiddling

indicators.note: fiddling means the letters of by egoistic are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Conservative idea is born of self-interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notion Tory' means a Tory notion. 'fiddling' rearranges BY and EGOISTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: David Cameron's Conservatives promoted this idea of community action replacing the state.

clue.text: 22 down is cracking — Picaroon's number one!

definitions.text: 22 down is cracking — Picaroon's number one!

indicators.note: is cracking means the letters of the other answer are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: the answer to the clue at 22 down, the throat swelling

indicators.note: number one means the first letter of the setter's name

explanation.surface: The setter boasts about his own clue being terrific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is cracking' scrambles GOITRE to EGOTRI; P is Picaroon's first letter. The clue praises the setter's own work.
explanation.definitionFit: Indulging in self-praise is an act of vanity, as when the setter calls himself number one.

clue.text: Try touching appeal at first — it may bring a lump to one's throat

definitions.text: it may bring a lump to one's throat

indicators.note: at first means the appeal piece comes before the touching piece

parts.note: to have a go is to try
it is sex appeal
re means about, touching

explanation.surface: A moving plea is tried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bring a lump to one's throat' looks emotional but is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A goitre is a swollen thyroid gland, which shows as a lump in the neck.

clue.text: Jittery touring soldiers, with others retreating, getting a pick-me-up

indicators.note: touring means the jittery word goes round the soldiers

parts.note: restive means fidgety, jittery
OR, other ranks, are soldiers

indicators.note: retreating means the other soldiers are read backwards

parts.note: other soldiers, the TA, the Territorial Army

explanation.surface: Nervous troops retreat with their comrades and need a tonic.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the British Territorial Army, here 'others' beside the first soldiers. 'retreating' turns TA to AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic that restores strength is a pick-me-up.

clue.text: Go over the top after soldiers

indicators.note: after means the top piece follows the soldiers

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers
a cap is the top of something

explanation.surface: Troops go over the top of the trench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go over the top' looks like going over the top of a trench; 'the top' is CAP.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to recapitulate, going over the main points again.

clue.text: One needing computer technology to comprehend 500 + 10?

definitions.text: One needing computer technology to comprehend 500 + 10?

indicators.note: to comprehend, to take in, means the computer letters hold the others inside

parts.note: IT is information technology, computer technology
D is 500 in Roman numerals
10 written in letters, I and O

explanation.surface: Someone needs a computer to work out a simple sum.
explanation.walkthrough: Partial &lit: 'One' gives no letters, and the whole clue paints the fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Only a dunce would need a computer to add up five hundred and ten.

clue.text: Japanese band love AC/DC

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
AC/DC is slang for bisexual, BI

explanation.surface: Someone adores the rock band AC/DC.
explanation.walkthrough: AC/DC and band suggest the rock group; band means a sash.
explanation.definitionFit: An obi is the broad sash worn round a kimono, a Japanese band of cloth.

clue.text: Some toast right-winger admitting defeat

indicators.note: admitting means the Conservative letters let the defeat word in

parts.note: Con is short for a Conservative, a right-winger
a rout is a heavy defeat

explanation.surface: A Tory toasts a defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some toast' suggests raising a glass; it is a piece of toasted bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A crouton is a small cube of toasted or fried bread, so it is a bit of toast.

clue.text: Duck has 0.1cm tongue

parts.note: a tenth of a centimetre is one millimetre, I MM
Erse is the Gaelic language, a tongue

explanation.surface: A duck has a tongue a millimetre long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the bird but is the verb, to dip under water.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck someone is to plunge them under water, the same as to immerse.

clue.text: Chapter hots up in novel with man who's a bit of a beast

definitions.text: man who's a bit of a beast

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of chapter hots up in take a new order

explanation.surface: A novel's chapter heats up with a brutish hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book, but it means new and signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An extinct ape-man once thought the missing link, half human, half animal.
